items.title: Carmen Caramanica interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, July 27, 2011
items.q: Norman Lear is going to be doing a show, he’s got a pilot, and it’s called “Different Strokes.”

ctx.x: No I think we did pretty good. I do have — back to the recording thing, with Tony Orlando we did a TV show called “Tony Orlando’s First Special.” It was for NBC. And the director was Alan Thicke. And so we did the show and I had a feature, a guitar feature. Well anyway, longer story, it was kind of a Spanish type thing on the song “Up on the Roof,” all right, and they had dancers and all this stuff they were going to do. So we did a pre-record in the studio and again I’m doing all these fancy jamming things over…

been on the gig for about two weeks. So the other guys in the band they’re looking at me like you apple polisher. Not why I did it. I just wanted to make sure that if I was down here and the music was up here that the guys at home wouldn’t look at me and say “you didn’t play that” or whatever. But anyway so I did that, and that came off okay. But then I went home to Utica, and about two days later Alan Thicke called up our musical director, Reg Powell, and said look, Norman Lear is going to be doing a show, he’s…
Right. You have to be able to show up in a hurry and take advantage of the opportunities and network and everything else. Wow. Well I’ve really enjoyed this conversation.
